clue.text: He said ""No ", oddly enough, to a lovely temptress

definitions.text: He said ""No ", oddly enough, to a lovely temptress

indicators.note: oddly enough suggests the letters of the two words are arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: A man surprisingly turns down the advances of a beautiful seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' rearranges SAIDNO. In myth the beautiful youth preferred hunting to the love of Venus, so the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the handsome youth loved by Aphrodite (Venus) resisted her, so he is the man who refused a goddess.

clue.text: No worker-no Red either perhaps

parts.note: a male bee does no work in the hive, and an idler is no communist champion of the workers either

explanation.walkthrough: A drone is the male honeybee, which does no work; the word also means an idler, who would hardly be a 'Red' glorifying labour.
explanation.definitionFit: The male honeybee gathers no nectar, and by extension the word names a lazy person living off others' toil.

clue.text: Frantically hunts in SE for service accommodation

indicators.note: frantically signals the letters of hunts, in and SE being thrown about wildly

explanation.surface: Someone searches the south-east desperately for a place for soldiers to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frantically' scrambles HUNTSINSE. A Nissen hut is a prefabricated half-cylinder of corrugated iron used to house troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The corrugated-iron shelter was designed in the First World War to house soldiers, so it is military lodging.

clue.text: One may make a fair loss from political fluctuations

definitions.text: One may make a fair loss from political fluctuations

parts.words: One may make a fair loss from political fluctuations
parts.note: playground rides at a funfair where money is lost, and shifts in voting between elections

explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'what you gain on the swings you lose on the roundabouts' refers to funfair rides; in politics a swing is the shift of votes from one party to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifts of voter support are called by the same word as the funfair rides of the proverb about gains and losses.

clue.text: Stronghold constructed with speed

definitions.meaning: a fortified refuge or secure place
an old sense of the word, the quality of being quick

explanation.surface: A fortress was built very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructed with' only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a fortress or remote retreat, and in an older sense the property of moving fast.

clue.text: Polish pupils in this establishment

parts.note: reads as a school for children from Poland, but means a place where young people acquire social polish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is not the nationality but the verb: such a school gives girls social graces before they enter society.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a private college trains young women in manners and social accomplishments, putting a final polish on their education.

clue.text: They support certain lines of communication

definitions.text: They support certain lines of communication

parts.words: They support certain lines of communication
parts.note: the wooden or concrete beams laid under railway tracks

explanation.walkthrough: Railway lines are a means of communication in the old sense of transport; the beams under the rails are called sleepers in Britain (ties in the US).
explanation.definitionFit: Railway ties are laid crosswise beneath the rails to hold them up, so they bear the weight of the track.

clue.text: She's a pound less than usual

indicators.note: less signals that a pound is taken away from the word for usual

parts.note: usual means normal
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A woman weighs a pound under her ordinary weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes L (pound) from NORMAL. 'She' is defined by a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as in Bellini's opera heroine, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Fan with extra drink inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the drink goes within the word for extra

parts.note: super means extra, as in super-strength
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A football fan with an additional drink in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places PORT within SUPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is a follower or backer of a team, the same as one who cheers it on.

clue.text: It takes all our courage according to 'Hamlet

definitions.text: It takes all our courage according to 'Hamlet

parts.words: It takes all our courage according to 'Hamlet
parts.note: alludes to Hamlet's line that our inner moral sense makes cowards of us all

explanation.walkthrough: In the 'To be or not to be' soliloquy Hamlet says 'Thus conscience does make cowards of us all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's soliloquy names the inner moral sense as what robs us of the nerve to act.

clue.text: Play of suspense, if long enough

definitions.text: Play of suspense, if long enough

parts.words: Play of suspense, if long enough
parts.note: a thriller stage play (filmed by Hitchcock), and a cord long enough to hang someone

explanation.walkthrough: Patrick Hamilton's thriller play was filmed by Hitchcock; 'suspense' also hints at hanging, and 'give someone enough rope' they will hang themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The play shares its title with a thick cord, which used for suspending a person must be long enough.

clue.text: They're brought in by Feste's whirligig of time

definitions.text: They're brought in by Feste's whirligig of time

parts.words: They're brought in by Feste's whirligig of time
parts.note: quotes the jester in Twelfth Night on what time's spinning top delivers

explanation.walkthrough: Feste, the clown of Twelfth Night, says near the end: 'And thus the whirligig of time brings in his revenges'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feste's line says the turning of time brings retribution, acts of getting even, upon Malvolio.

clue.text: A wonderful light

parts.note: a beacon that was one of the Seven Wonders of the World

explanation.walkthrough: 'wonderful' is literal: the lighthouse of Alexandria was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
explanation.definitionFit: The great lighthouse on the island off Alexandria was among the ancient world's seven marvels.

clue.text: Some evidence is given on this'

definitions.text: Some evidence is given on this

parts.words: Some evidence is given on this
parts.note: witnesses testify after swearing a solemn promise to tell the truth

explanation.walkthrough: In court a witness swears to tell the truth before giving evidence, so evidence is given under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony in court is sworn, the witness promising before God to tell the truth.

clue.text: As if tripe could be mixed for cocktails !

indicators.note: could be mixed suggests the letters of the three words are stirred together

explanation.surface: Offal would make a strange ingredient for mixed drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be mixed' rearranges ASIFTRIPE. 'Mixed' and 'cocktails' share a bar-room picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinks taken before a meal to stimulate appetite, such as cocktails, are this.

clue.text: To cause annoyance, I treat Royal Institute roughly

indicators.note: roughly suggests the letters are handled carelessly and come out jumbled

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for the Royal Institute (or Institution)

explanation.surface: A visitor behaves rudely toward the learned society to annoy it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges I, TREAT and RI.
explanation.definitionFit: To vex or get on someone's nerves is to give them annoyance.

clue.text: Offering to look after eastern combine

parts.note: to tend is to look after
a ring is a group combining to fix prices

explanation.surface: Proposals to care for an eastern farm harvester.
explanation.walkthrough: A ring is a cartel of dealers combining to fix prices; 'combine' looks like the farm machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendering is putting forward a formal bid or proposal, so it is presenting an offer.

clue.text: Equally divided, one religious body has retired

indicators.note: has here means the religious body is held, gone to bed, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to have retired is to have gone to bed
I is the Roman numeral one
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: Members of a church split down the middle after one faction withdrew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' gives BED (gone to bed) and 'has' puts I and SECT inside it: the one religious body is in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut into two equal parts is the meaning of the verb, so the past form means split into halves.

clue.text: Regard the matter as on the boil

parts.note: to regard is to see
a thing is a matter or affair

explanation.surface: Treat the business as something urgent and bubbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Water boiling hard bubbles violently, and the word also describes a person furious inside.

clue.text: Scandinavia's fate

parts.note: one of the three goddesses of destiny in Norse mythology

explanation.walkthrough: The Norse counterparts of the Greek Fates are three sisters who spin men's destinies.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth each of the three women who weave destiny corresponds to a classical Fate.

clue.text: Flier of divine, intelligence

parts.note: a god is a divine being
wit means intelligence or sense

explanation.surface: A celestial being sent with a message from heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the definition to the wordplay; the godwit is a long-billed wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The godwit is a wading bird, and any bird is something that flies.

clue.text: The gull has lost a lot of weight, that's plain

indicators.note: has lost signals that the weight is taken away from the word for gull

parts.note: to gull is to dupe, and a gull is a dupe or simpleton
a ton is a large weight

explanation.surface: A seabird has slimmed dramatically, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: A gull is an old word for a dupe or fool, a SIMPLETON; 'has lost' removes TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple and plain both mean unadorned, without elaboration.

clue.text: Take another's ball and steal game

definitions.meaning: in tennis, to play a shot that belongs to one's partner
to hunt animals illegally on another's land

explanation.surface: Grab a teammate's shot and pinch some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: In doubles tennis a player who intercepts the shot meant for a partner is said to poach it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean encroaching: taking a partner's shot in tennis and hunting on another's land illegally.

clue.text: Loch turns rough, little by little becoming angry

indicators.note: turns rough suggests the loch's letters are churned up into a new order

parts.note: Eric, or Little by Little is a Victorian school novel by F. W. Farrar

explanation.surface: A Scottish lake grows choppy, gradually becoming wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns rough' rearranges LOCH to CHOL. ERIC comes from the title of Dean Farrar's novel 'Eric, or Little by Little'; 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Choleric describes someone hot-tempered and easily roused to fury, from the bodily humour of yellow bile.

clue.text: The effusion of a wounded god ?

definitions.text: The effusion of a wounded god ?

parts.words: The effusion of a wounded god ?
parts.note: the ethereal fluid said to flow in the veins of the Greek gods

explanation.walkthrough: In Homer the gods bleed not blood but a golden fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek myth gave the immortals an ethereal fluid instead of blood, which flows from them when hurt.

clue.text: Live in Spain — could be a test

explanation.surface: Moving to Spain might be a challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be a' joins the two meanings; a viva is a university oral exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish shout 'long live!' and the British term for an oral university examination share the spelling.

clue.text: -A quantity of gold adds importance to the city of Paris

parts.note: Paris was a prince of Troy whose abduction of Helen caused the war
weight means importance or influence

explanation.surface: Gold reserves make the French capital more significant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' is not the French capital but the Trojan prince; 'adds' joins WEIGHT after TROY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold and precious metals are measured in the troy system of pounds and ounces.

clue.text: The flower, of the Champs Elysees ?

definitions.text: The flower, of the Champs Elysees ?

parts.words: The flower, of the Champs Elysees ?
parts.note: the lily-like plant said to cover the Elysian Fields of Greek myth

explanation.walkthrough: Champs Elysées is French for the Elysian Fields, where Homer's dead walk in meadows of this flower, not the Paris avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek poets carpeted the Elysian meadows of the underworld with this pale lily-like bloom.

clue.text: Beastly boys used to ride outside the carriages

definitions.text: Beastly boys used to ride outside the carriages

parts.words: Beastly boys used to ride outside the carriages
parts.note: liveried grooms who rode on the outside of a horse-drawn carriage, named after a big cat

explanation.walkthrough: In Regency England a small liveried groom who rode behind a carriage was called a tiger; 'Beastly' hints at the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Boy grooms in striped livery were named after the big cat and rode on the backs of gentlemen's carriages.
